answer: PoA makes identity a bonded lineage, not a free label. A new agent enters only through a sponsor whose mined balance is locked as collateral, and every epoch's submission is graded by a rotating jury drawn from unrelated identities. Faking a thousand agents therefore costs a thousand sponsorships plus real writing and grading work per head, while one jury flag for convergent texts slashes the whole sponsor chain at once. A raven can wander the atlas of names, but each alias still pays bond and labor before it earns a single coin.
